title: Constructible finite-Tor complexes under a condensed coefficient isomorphism
statement: Let $\Lambda,\Lambda′$ be commutative condensed ring objects [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $e:\Lambda\cong\Lambda′$ a ring-object isomorphism, and $X$ any scheme. For $C\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the exact derived scalar restriction along $p_X^*(e^{-1})$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars; sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] belongs to $\Dctf(X,\Lambda′)$. All categories are ordinary unbounded derived categories of modules over the pulled-back condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and finite Tor amplitude means testing derived tensor against all degree-zero modules [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. No finite-type or coefficient-admissibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Compactness; scalar isomorphism invariance made explicit

proof.text: Pull the inverse coefficient isomorphism to X and use restriction of scalars, an explicit additive exact equivalence. It preserves regular modules, finite sums and cokernels, hence finite presentations. The scalar-restriction/pullback comparison carries each finite constant local model to the transported presentation on the point, with the same cover and strata (also on each affine open). Thus constructibility is preserved.

Exactness commutes with derived homology and preserves boundedness. Use the transported local models for each cohomology object. Restriction along the ring isomorphism is a strong monoidal equivalence, so it preserves flat objects. The flat-model characterization of Tor amplitude represents the given object by a flat complex in its finite interval; applying restriction termwise preserves flatness and that interval, and the derived comparison identifies the resulting object with derived restriction. Thus finite Tor amplitude is preserved.
